The largest current resize gap is the existing bounded byte2×9 control:
1,338.67/zimg1,049.55µs, upper1.280,114B/op. Its production path is unchanged
by the [shared byte-geometry round](BYTE-CROSS-SHARED-GEOMETRY.md); that source-valid

One two-second CPU0 operation/CPU1 sampler capture contains1,998 instruction
locations:1,241 in `GeneratedBicubicResize.FilterRow`,731 in

`FilterRow` reconstructs the same eight-tap coefficient vectors and clamped
positions for each needed source row. The proposed next stage filters a bounded
group of source rows together, preparing each coefficient/index/pair-vector block
once for that group. Preserve every row's original tap order and lower-then-upper
adds, the original vertical-coordinate order and repeated clamped contributions,
normalization/magnitudes, coefficient verification, certificates and exact repair.

Verify explicit storage and nested repair overlap before choosing block sizes.
Use the existing4KiB admission, with cancellation through actual users and no
fallback after refusal. Interleaving may increase cache/register pressure; counts
alone authorize no merge. Existing2×2/1×1 byte controls share the generated regime
and must reconcile if affected. No new matrix, full-height cache, coefficient table,
pool, codec session or approximate numerical policy.
